title: Excellent Audio Extension Cable
text:
One of the frequent frustrations with headphones is the limited cord length of the phones - typically about 3'. Bluetooth is one way around this - an inexpensive receiver can turn a good set of wired phones into a wireless pair - but this is not always practical. An extension cable is a much more practical solution in many situations and is a lot less expensive in most cases. This extender cable is one of the better ones I have used.

This is not a cheap, basic audio cable. It is a heavier-gauge wire encased in braided nylon insulation. Though braided nylon is becoming more common, plastic coating is still the standard and in my experience the nylon braid holds up under heavy use much better. More interesting are the plugs on the end of the cable, though - instead of just a molded plastic grip on the end, this cable has a substantial metal cap that screws down and gives the whole cap much more sturdiness. This won’t help with constant sharp tugging at a tight angle but it does all but eliminate most stresses on the plug.

I should mention that this cable is for stereo audio only and does not work for replacing a cable used for talk (never mind that there’s no microphone). It will work with other cables that are set up for talk, but once this cable is in the mix the ability to talk goes away. That’s not a defect but a design decision. So, if you plan to use this to extend the reach of a two-way headset it will not work.

This particular cable is 6' and I have it connected to my headphones and that gives me much more range to move around my work area.

This is a very good audio cable. It works as it is supposed to work and it is designed to last much longer than the average cable. This is an excellent choice if you need an audio-only cable that will not wear out or break quickly.

title: Very pleased with this phone (upgraded from a Note 2)
text:
First off: If you are upgrading from another Android or even an Apple phone here is some advice you may find useful. Search Samsung's site for an app called Samsung Smart Switch. If for some reason that app fails you, move all of your text messages from your old phone to this one by loading a free app called [[ASIN:B0075A5S0K SMS Backup & Restore]] and following the directions I outlined in my November 30, 2013 review of that product. Another free app you may want to consider is [[ASIN:B006FJMDTG Software Data Cable]], which allows you to back up your old Android phone to a laptop or PC, then move it to your new phone from that backup. You will need to load that app on your old phone and the Note 3, but it's simple and very handy.

I'll attempt to not parrot the excellent and informative reviews that have already been posted. I do want to share my experiences with this phone and the ease of moving from the Note 2 to this model.

The first thing I noticed is despite the small differences in size, the screen on this one if brighter, has more vivid colors and can be easily viewed in direct sunlight. That alone made my upgrade worth it.

A second thing is this is a faster phone. I do not use it to anywhere near its capacity, but it zips along from one screen or app to the next with no lag. I was more than pleased with my older Note 2, but this one is even better.

Having 32GB of internal storage is a treat, especially since I have a 64GB external SD card to augment it. That comes to 16GB more storage than my 80GB laptop, so it's easy to forecast that the next version of this phone could finally wean me off computers. As it is I am spending a lot more time on my phone doing stuff I use to do on my computer.

I appreciate the greatly improved camera resolution and the easier and more intuitive interface, but that is icing on the cake. What I truly love is even though this one runs under Android 4.3 versus 4.1.2 on my Note 2, there are no major differences in the user interface. In that respect there was zero learning curve. After tweaking a few settings that did not come over when I restored my old ones, I was up and running as before in practically no time.

While this ships with a cable that supports USB 3.0 and has what looks like a connector that is incompatible with existing micro USB chargers, that is not the case. You can still use existing chargers, battery packs and the such because their micro USB connectors will plug into one side of the charging port. If you have a computer capable of USB 3.0 your transfer rates will be lightning fast.

With respect to battery, the Note 3 is about par with the Note 2 for use time between charges. Since the Note 3's 4.3 Android operating system does include Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) support you may notice a slightly improved use time if you use bluetooth a lot. As it stands there is a very slight difference between the Note 2's 3100mAh battery capacity and the 3200mAh one in this phone.

I am still exploring the nuances of my new phone, so as I discover noteworthy features that I have missed or emergent problems that I should warn about I will update this review to reflect them. In the meantime, if you are considering an upgrade to the Note 3 from the previous model and are wondering if it's worth it - I say yes. Read the other reviews for other perspectives and information too because combined there is a high level of customer satisfaction.

title: Awesome camera! My review includes tips should you have issues accessing the ADMIN page...
text:
Feels like a very solid camera in terms of build quality. Nice and hefty. Everybody's networking ability is different. Some may find this very difficult to set up, some may find it a breeze. I hit a snag, and was SMH for awhile, but I figured it out, and I'll share with you my issue, and how I solved it. So if you happen to run into the same issue, these notes may help.

So H.View provides you with an ADMIN IP address which should work once your camera is connected to your home network. In this case, it's 192.168.1.120. You punch this into you browser, and you should be able to get to the ADMIN page to change your password and view your camera. But what happens when this IP address doesn't work for you? You will need to change it accordingly to your IPV4 gateway. I found out the easiest way is to simply let the IPC Manager modify it automatically by DHCP. I posted 3 screenshots to hopefully guide you. Here are some worthy notes...

1. Google "IPC Manager H.View" to find your way to their site to download the software. Top result with the headline DOWNLOAD CENTER should be the correct one. Be sure to download the version for your device, Linux, Mac, or Windows. BTW, they keep this in a Google Drive folder, so don't worry, you're in the right place.

2. Connect your camera to your network via POE switch. This set DOES NOT come with a power adapter, it is meant for POE switch users.

3. Install and launch the software and login in the lower left corner. Default is ADMIN and 12345. You can change this later. The login is strange because it doesn't give any feedback. Usually after logging in to a software, something changes or refreshes, such as a "log out" option, this lets you know you're logged in. But there seems to be no reaction in this software. After you hit enter, nothing changes. So don't fret, you're really logged in.

4. If you don't see any cameras, right click and hit refresh. Once you see your camera, check the box to SELECT your camera. Now, if you right click on your camera, there is a menu with a "OPEN HOME" option. If you click this, it "should" launch you to the admin page at 192.168.1.120, where you can change your password and view the camera. You can also manually punch the ip address in your browser.

5. This is where I ran into a snag. The default IP did not work for me. The browser would load an error page, "This site could not be reached." Proceed to #6 if you encounter this issue...

6. Go back into the IPC software. Make sure the default login credentials are still present, make sure your Camera is still Selected. Now, SELECT the DHCP box, and hit MODIFICATION. There should be a pop-up indicating the modification was successful. The IP address should now have changed from 192.168.1.120 to whatever new address that your router assigned. If it's still the same, try hitting refresh.

7. So now, you right click on your camera and hit OPEN HOME again, and you should be able to get to the admin page now. Or as mentioned before, just manually punch in the new IP address into your browser. When you successfully reach the admin page for the first time, you will be prompted to change your password. Now you can view your camera. Next time you go back tin the IPC software, make sure to use your new password.

I included 3 screenshots to supplement these notes. Hope that helps! This is a 5-Star product!

title: High quality camera, but it runs very hot currently...
text:
Okay, you know the saying about first impressions? Presentation matters in a "premium" product. Anything north of $200, I expect good packaging. This Panacast is priced over $500 and has a retail of nearly a $1000. This is iPhone territory, yet the thin cardboard box with creases looks like packaging you'd find on any other white label gadget coming outta China. It was smushed a little cause it was shipped in an Amazon white padded envelope. If it weren't for the fact that this is a Vine item for me, I'd be so upset.

As for the camera itself, it is pretty nifty and the quality is what you'd expect for something over $500. It is small, but when you hold it in your hands, you feel the heft of the metal. It is definitely not one of those cheap lightweight plastic cameras. However, they got to do something about the heat. After a few minutes, you can fry eggs with it. It runs hot! I hope future firmware can do something about this.

There is nothing obvious in terms of picture or video quality that would separate this from the $100 stuff on the market. They all look the same to me. The 180 degree is the reason you're getting this. If you download their JabraDirect software, you'll have more control over the camera. For instance, you can lock in at a certain degree. I like to play around with the 180 degree, so initially I was annoyed that it kept automatically zooming in and out on me due to movement. The desktop software will allow you to lock in on any degree you want. I'm sure this will make a fine camera for business settings, but for us, it's simply for video calls with relatives overseas. Grandparents will often say, "what's my little boy doing over there?" Well, now they get to have a wider view.

The price, the underwhelming packaging, and the heat issue... I'm knocking 2 stars.

title: Does not work with calls, but otherwise great!
text:
This is a great way to continue using your wired headphones without giving up your charging port. It is a little bulkier than a straight USB-to-3.5mm adapter, but that's just how it has to be in order to make room for two plugs on a dongle like this.
A couple of things to note: The USB cable does not support data, only charging. But that's expected since it says so on this listing.
The thing that DID surprise me, however, is that it does not support the inline mic for calls. During a test phone call, the audio was coming from the phone's mic and not the headset, which we confirmed by tapping on the mic and then again on the phone (only the phone tap sound was heard). It actually says for calls on the listing, which I believe is a mistake. I'm guessing this unit supports TRS and ignores the extra pin for TRRS, so it's great for listening to music only and this is why I'm removing one star.

title: Kid tested, parent approved!
text:
[[VIDEOID:ef18b2bc61d2bf43363a5f3d51e2b5d8]] This is a pretty great tablet geared for kids. Inside of the "kid-proof" case is an Android 11 powered tablet with a comfortable-to-read 10" display, much better than the 7" Kindle Fire tablet that my kids used to use before this. It has the standard Google play store, yet still comes with plenty of parental control tools and a pretty great suite of software for kid friendly use (something I really liked about the Kindle OS).
It even comes with a USB OTG plug so that you can plug in accessories like a USB sticks, a keyboard or barcode scanner, etc.
The only thing that bothered me a little bit is that the case makes the buttons and USB port a little bit difficult to line up. To turn on and off the power, for example, you need to find the on button next to the volume buttons, which isn't immediately easy for a kid to find. I can imagine younger ones especially hitting every other button first. And the OTG adapter had some trouble fitting in the hole cutaway since the port didn't sit exactly in the middle of the case. The cameras were also cheap-phone quality, but then again I never expect good camera performance at this price range.
That being said, it does an excellent job at what it is designed to do: Be a kind friendly tablet that parents will be happy about.

title: Great way to store your gear
text:
I work in photo/video for a living, so cases like these to travel with are an absolute necessity. They feel relatively tough and rugged, however I hope that I never have to test the waterproof claim. When I first opened it, the rubber lining that I believe is used to keep it water tight was actually half detached and hanging. I had to feed it back into the groove it fits into, where it has stayed since. That's OK as I don't intend for this to suffer more than some light rain heading to/from a gig rather than survive a flood, but if the waterproof claim is what piqued your interest, perhaps a brand like Pelican would be a better wager.
Otherwise, this is a very decent and usable case for things I want to protect, such as lenses, batteries, microphones, etc.
NOTE: I was hoping my DJI Phantom 3 would fit in one of these, but it does not. I could have measured ahead of time and known that, but I got excited seeing the images here of others fitting their (smaller) drones in. The Phantom drones need a bigger case, unfortunately.

title: Quite Surprising Sound For This Price Range Of Headphones With A Few Disappointments
text:
I was looking for some replacement headphones for two sets in my family when I had the opportunity to try out some of the new Carlos Santana line of headphones. Let's see what happened.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These headphones come in a great box which will appeal to fans of Carlose. It is well decorated and presentation is done so well, it would make a great gift. These are the black ones, and there is also another set available in white under a different listing.

ARE THESE REAL LEATHER?
According to the case,t these are leather padded ear cups and the lower half of the headband. I am still not sure about this. It is possibly bonded leather. Bonded leather is made from leather scraps chopped up and blended with binders. Sheets made of this mixture are printed with leather look imprinting. Technically it can be called leather, but it really is not leather as I define it..

EAR CUSHIONS AND HEADBAND
These black headphones are comfortable. I can wear these headphones longer than many others I have used. My daughter who ended up with these, uses them constantly and raves about them. These can be worn for several hours without a problem. She has sweaty ears and these are not nearly as frustrating for her as many others.

CORD FOR CORDED LISTENING
This comes with a cord which is only 38 inches long. That is a bit short for me. I find it is annoying and not quite as long as I would prefer, but my daughter does not use it so I guess it is not a problem for her or if you are like her, you won't mind either.

HOW DO THESE SOUND?
We are all surprised at how really good these sound. The bass is well defined and clear/strong, and the mids and highs are definitely clear and not muddy. The bass is not overwhelming either, which is a problem with some headphones.

HEADPHONE CONTROLS
The controls can be a bit difficult to read, but once you know where they are, you can figure it out pretty quickly. The +/- and play/pause buttons are separated by the noise cancellation button which is good.

HOW ARE THESE ADJUSTABLE?
These adapt to all sorts of comfortable positions.. They go longer, tilt in and out and rotate from side to side.

ARE THESE ABLE TO FOLD TO BE COMPACT?
These do fold flat and compact if you need to travel with them or store them in a smaller storage area.

CASE?
This did not come with a case.

SOUND CANCELLATION PERFORMANCE
The noise cancellation is awful. It hardly works. When noise cancellation is turned on, the sound gets pretty compromised. It becomes almost muffled in a way and the base definitely goes down.

OTHER FEATURES WITH THESE HEADPHONES
The ability to know how much power is left on the headphones while using the phone is nice, but it does not help if you are using these some other bluetooth device and not a phone. During phone calls, people hear just fine and we can hear them too (several of us tried this feature with our phones)

THE BOTTOM LINE
At this price point, these headphones are a step up from what I usually get when getting headphones for this price range. The sound is well defined and well balanced. Compactness for storage is great, and the comfort is also very good. The only disappointments are noise cancellation, short cord for corded listening, and buttons being a bit difficult to read.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. With better performance from noise cancellation, these would be really really good. As they are, they are still pretty great. They are a great gift to yourself or someone else and are some of the nicer headphones I have used in my journey through headphones of all sorts as well as those the family has obtained. They are not B&O or Turtle Beach, but they still are pretty good.
